\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Basic}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Basic
\section{Overview}
Affine hypercontractivity is defined for real random variables and extended norm exponents. Symmetric and Rademacher laws, finite atom support, multilinear evaluation, and moment identities provide the common probability-space framework.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Affine hypercontractivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive}
\leanok
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p256-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p272-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p272-b003
}
For a real function $X$ on a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ and extended exponents $p,q\in[0,\infty]$, $(p,q,\rho)$-hypercontractivity means $1\le p\le q$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for every $a,b\in\bbr$, with extended-valued norms and the essential supremum at infinity.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Real-valued random-variable norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm}
\leanok
For a real function $X$ on a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $q\in\bbr$, define $N_q(X)$ by taking the extended norm at exponent $\max(q,0)$ and converting it to a real number; a finite value is retained and an infinite value is assigned $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Symmetric random variable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsSymmetricRV}
\leanok
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{pdf-681b6f3d947f-p153-b003}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p279-b001}
A real function $X$ on a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ is symmetric when $X$ and $-X$ are almost everywhere measurable and have the same distribution under $\mu$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Rademacher random variable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsRademacherRV}
\leanok
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p023-b003,
  pdf-681b6f3d947f-p153-b003
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p259-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p259-b006
}
A Rademacher variable on a measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$ is a measurable $r:\Omega\to\bbr$ satisfying $r\in\{-1,1\}$ almost everywhere and $\mu(r=1)=\mu(r=-1)=1/2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Random-input multilinear evaluation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p032-b001}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p020-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p022-b002
}
Let $F$ assign a real coefficient $F(S)$ to every $S\subseteq[n]$, and let $X_i:\Omega\to\bbr$. Define $F(X)(\omega)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i(\omega)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lower bounds on finite atoms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.HasAtomLowerBound}
\leanok
A real function $X$ on $(\Omega,\mu)$ has atom lower bound $\lambda\in\bbr$ when there exists a finite $s\subseteq\bbr$ supporting $X$ almost everywhere and every $x\in s$ satisfies $\mu(X=x)\ge\max(\lambda,0)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Power integral formula for the norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm}
\difficulty{3}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be any measure space, let $q>0$, and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$
belong to $L^q(\mu)$. Then $N_q(X)^q=\int_\Omega |X(\omega)|^q\,d\mu(\omega)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Squared norm of a centered affine function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_affine_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_rpow}
\difficulty{5}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ belong to
$L^2(\mu)$ with mean zero. For all $a,b\in\mathbb R$, the real-valued random-variable
norm satisfies $N_2(a+bX)^2=a^2+b^2N_2(X)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Law of a Rademacher variable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsRademacherRV.map_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsRademacherRV}
\statementsource{vershynin-hdp-book}{pdf-681b6f3d947f-p153-b003}
\difficulty{5}
Let $r$ be a measurable random variable on a probability space, with $r\in\{-1,1\}$ almost surely and $\Pr[r=1]=\Pr[r=-1]=1/2$. Its law is $\tfrac12\delta_1+\tfrac12\delta_{-1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conjugate affine contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive.conjugate}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_rpow}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p259-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p259-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p259-b003
}
\difficulty{6}
Let $X$ be centered on a probability space, let $q>2$, and suppose $H_{2,q,\rho}(X)$. Then $H_{q/(q-1),2,\rho}(X)$. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
\end{theorem}

Let $(␀␀)$ be a measure space, let $X$ be a real-valued function on it, and suppose $X$

\begin{theorem}[Reducing the contraction radius]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive.mono_radius}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p256-b004,

}
\difficulty{6}
Let $X$ be centered on a probability space, suppose $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$, and let $0\le\sigma\le\rho$. Then $H_{p,q,\sigma}(X)$, including extended exponents equal to infinity. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite atomic support implies integrability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.HasAtomLowerBound.memLp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.HasAtomLowerBound}
\difficulty{3}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a measurable space with a finite measure, and let
$X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable. Suppose there is a finite set $s\subseteq\mathbb
R$ such that $X$ lies in $s$ almost everywhere and, for every $x\in s$,
$\mu(\{\omega:X(\omega)=x\})\ge\max(\lambda,0)$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. Then $X$
belongs to $L^p(\mu)$ for every extended nonnegative real exponent $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth moments of multilinear evaluations]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV_memLp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV_memLp_nat, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p250-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p250-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p251-b002
}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be mutually independent real random variables on a probability space, each belonging to $L^4$. For arbitrary real coefficients $F(S)$, the multilinear evaluation $\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ belongs to $L^4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Moment algebra inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.reasonable_moment_algebra}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $R,a,b,A,D,C\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $9\le R$, $0\le a$, $0\le b$, $0\le C$, $0\le D$,
$A\le Ra^2$, $D\le b^2$, and $C^2\le AD$. Then $A+6C+RD\le R(a+b)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Splitting a multilinear sum]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.multilinear_sum_insert}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a set, let $\iota$ be an index set, let $s\subseteq\iota$ be finite, and
choose $i\in\iota\setminus s$. Let $F$ assign a real coefficient to each finite subset
of $\iota$, and let $X_j:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ for each $j\in\iota$. For every
$\omega\in\Omega$, the sum over subsets of $s\cup\{i\}$ satisfies
\[\sum_{T\subseteq s\cup\{i\}}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)=\sum_{T\subseteq s}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)+X_i(\omega)\sum_{T\subseteq s}F(T\cup\{i\})\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega).\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integrability of products of powers]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrable_mul_pow_of_memLp}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a measurable space with a finite measure, and let
$f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ belong to $L^p(\mu)$ for a natural number $p$. If $a,b$ are
natural numbers with $a+b\le p$, then the function $\omega\mapsto f(\omega)^a
g(\omega)^b$ is integrable with respect to $\mu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hypercontractivity Under Identical Distribution]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive.identDistrib}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive.identDistrib}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Xi,\nu)$ be measure spaces, and let $X:\Omega\to\bbr$ and
$Y:\Xi\to\bbr$ be identically distributed with respect to these measures. If $X$ is
$(p,q,\rho)$-hypercontractive under $\mu$, then $Y$ is $(p,q,\rho)$-hypercontractive
under $\nu$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Norm of a constant random variable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_const}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_const}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm}
\difficulty{3}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $c,q\in\mathbb R$, and suppose $q>0$. The
real-valued random-variable norm of the constant function with value $c$ is
$N_q(c)=|c|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Homogeneity of the random-variable norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_const_mul}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_const_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm}
\difficulty{3}
For any measure space $(\Omega,\mu)$, any real-valued function $X$ on $\Omega$, and any
$c,q\in\mathbb R$, the real-valued random-variable norm satisfies $N_q(cX)=|c|N_q(X)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integrability of multilinear random evaluation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV_memLp_nat}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV_memLp_nat}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p$ be a positive natural number, and let
$(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space. Suppose $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent
real-valued random variables on this space, each belonging to $L^p(\mu)$. Then for every
real coefficient family $F$ indexed by subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the random
variable $\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}} F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ belongs to
$L^p(\mu)$.
\end{theorem}
